text:
anya: Heads-up — during staging hardening I found an alert from the keystore agent on our private deploy. wondering what the expected RBAC + audit path is before I escalate.
sam: Can you paste the alert? is this the agent that talks to our KMS shim?
anya: yep. sec-bot reported: "keystore-agent: failed decrypt 403 -> missing keystore.decrypt permission". stack trace short: `agent/keystore.go:142 -> kmsclient.Decrypt -> 403`.
liam: interesting. that sounds like an RBAC regression from the last role sync. did you roll any service-account changes?
anya: I rolled a tighter role template to remove wildcard decrypt perms for long-lived svcaccs yesterday. i tested in sandbox but not the onprem cluster.
priya: If the agent is missing decrypt, it should still log the attempt to local audit (audit.log) and trigger our alert. do we see local audit entries?
anya: yes, /var/log/redwood/keystore-audit.log shows entries: `[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] svcacc=redwood-keystore-agent action=Decrypt resource=kek-01 result=DENIED reason=rbac-policy`
dmitri: That confirms RBAC prevented a decrypt, not KMS auth failure. Good. Two quick asks: 1) what minimal RBAC perms allow agent to operate in a private deploy? 2) what's the recommended audit policy (retention + fields) for onprem?
sam: Minimal perms: keystore-agent needs (kms:Decrypt) scoped to the key ARN /key-id and a narrow principal binding to the agent's service account. On k8s this is an RBAC + IRSA style mapping — for our private installs we map the svcacc to the keystore role via the node bootstrap. Example policy snippet: `{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":["arn:cloud:kms:region:acct:key/kek-01"]}]}`
liam: add network constraint: only allow the agent pod to talk to KMS via the keystore-proxy IP range. enforce with NetworkPolicy egress rule so even if svcacc has perms, egress is limited to proxy endpoints.
priya: Audit policy: log principal, svcacc, request payload hash (not raw material), key id, action, result, trace_id, and peer cert fingerprint. Retain 90 days hot, 1 year cold, FHIR/PCI customers may need longer. Our local format: `ts|svcacc|action|key|result|trace` — make sure logs are append-only and sent to central collector when network allows.
anya: For the onprem install, we can't ship logs outside of customer network by default. plan is to write to append-only file and expose a pull API for support with signed one-time tokens. ok?
dmitri: Sounds right for privacy. Also consider an audit checksum chain to detect tampering: stamp each file with HMAC using a rotation key stored in HSM/KMS.
sec-bot: [automated] detection: keystore-agent-decrypt-denied count=4 window=5m severity=warning rule=rbac-mismatch path=/srv/agents/keystore
sam: Given this is a staging harden, mitigation path: 1) re-add temporary least-privileged decrypt permission to agent's role scoped to key; 2) patch role sync to exclude that role from the tighter template; 3) run smoke e2e decrypt test; 4) then separately tighten network egress and add netpol.
liam: I can craft a minimal NetworkPolicy for us to apply on prem. quick draft: ```yaml apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: keystore-agent-egress spec: podSelector: matchLabels: app: keystore-agent policyTypes: [Egress] egress: - to: - ipBlock: cidr: 10.20.30.0/24 ports: - protocol: TCP port: 443 ``` This limits egress to our keystore-proxy subnet.
priya: Also enable kube-audit admission plugin to record the svcacc->role binding changes. we saw role-sync changed templates; that should be auditable. set audit policy to capture `create`/`update` for Role/ClusterRoleBindings at RequestLevel=Metadata.
anya: I pushed a quick rollback to staging role-bindings, re-ran keystore smoke. decrypt now succeeds. leaving the log entries for triage.
dmitri: Next steps for permanent fix: - add a stage gate in infra-pipeline that runs `keystore smoke` after any RBAC template PR - require netpol + egress whitelist as part of Private deploy baseline - add audit HMAC chain for onprem logs - add a documented fallback: if keystore fails, agent should return sanitized error and route requests to secondary key set (no plaintext leakage).
sam: For incident response, if a customer reports denied decrypts: 1) ask for audit slice (trace_id) 2) check RBAC diff for the svcacc 3) check netpol egress 4) if we must, temporarily grant decrypt via a short-lived role and rotate keys after resolution. document that with approval flow.
anya: I'll open a short RFC with the minimal policy + netpol + audit HMAC plan. tagging @sam @dmitri for review.
liam: ack, I'll add the netpol PR.
priya: i'll prepare the audit retention doc and HSM HMAC note.
sec-bot: [automated] ticket created: SEC-2026-154 keystore-agent-rbac-mismatch
anya: thanks all :thumbsup:
